speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions and how long they have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent exposure to chickenpox and the description of painless, nonpruritic papules, are the lesions firm, dome-shaped, and do they have a central dimple or umbilication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum contagiosum, a viral skin infection common in young children. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
